scientific_review: 407 source ensembles reduce to183 occupied1km cells with no empty cells;57 eastward steps reflect station-stop/drift behavior. One native profile nearest each spatial cell center is used, ties earliest, avoiding time-dwell weighting. This is an explicit sample-selection scenario, not recovered author interpolation.

Nine PG/window combinations retain signed native V and native depth coordinates. Centered uniform means require at least5 contributors,80percent ensemble support and60percent spatial span. Horizontally incomplete edge windows and empty centers cannot produce a synthetic maximum; no vertical filling or surface extrapolation.

Two shallow positive peaks separated by at least40km define a provisional pair; the intervening minimum defines a source-informed split. Independent source S2 polygon membership has not been recovered, so western/inshore and eastern/main remain candidate classes.

Offshore maximum depth is40.44m at15/25km windows and128.44m at35km for all three PG selections. Inshore maxima vary with window and PG, including288.44m at25km PG50/70 versus168.44m PG90. These are native sampled scenario values, not physical accuracy, statistical bounds or seasonal depth changes.
Source Table3 and individual crossing prose retain different scopes and unresolved processing/aggregation. No exact source reproduction or explanation of their difference is claimed.

Near-bottom/sidelobe masking and archive tide correction remain unverified. Original Figure12 pixels show a steep shelf edge, so PG alone cannot authorize canonical inshore core admission. Physical bottoms, thickness, whole-route profiles and volumes remain unknown.

Nine cloud tests cover peak/minimum splitting, unresolved peaks, signed smoothing and edge exclusion, missing/low-PG samples, native vertical gaps, edge maxima/unknown bottoms, ties, station revisits and empty spatial centers. Raw archive hash and8MiB retrieval bound are retained. No local ocean-field processing or local tests.
